title: The Computational Architecture of the Fraserphere Beyond Power Scaling
abstract: The Computational Architecture of the Fraserphere Beyond Power Scaling Author: Kyle Ross Fraser Affiliation: Independent Researcher Date: July 3, 2026 Abstract A recent critique correctly observed that correcting the arithmetic consistency between node count and collection fraction in the Fraserphere scaling analysis does not, by itself, constitute a computational theory. The objection states that the work reduces to power collection calculations “dressed as an AI result,” lacking a memory model, interconnect budget, defined operations, and any mechanism that actually links distributed operations per second to cognition. This report addresses that objection directly. It specifies the missing architectural layers: a photonic node design with explicit memory and primitive operations, a delay-aware interconnect strategy grounded in predictive processing, and a three-tier NeuroSwarms emergence mechanism in which local photonic inference, medium-scale coordination, and slow global model alignment together implement distributed active inference across stellar distances. The power calculations are treated as necessary infrastructure rather than the central claim. The architecture is presented as a coherent, if still largely conceptual, proposal for stellar-scale cognition rather than generic compute. Introduction The critique in question reads, in essence: arithmetic self-consistency has been achieved, yet the project still contains “no computational architecture: no memory model, no interconnect budget, no defined operation, no mechanism linking distributed ops/s to cognition.” It further warns that iterative refinement with language models tends to patch internal numerical consistency while leaving the fundamental leap from power to cognition untouched. The observation that power accounting alone is insufficient is correct. Energy is a constraint, not a theory of computation. However, the further claim that the Fraserphere framework has never supplied (or cannot supply) the missing architectural elements is not. The following sections articulate those elements, drawing on the conceptual development of the Fraserphere as a photonic, delay-tolerant, multi-scale active inference system. The goal is not to claim empirical validation, but to demonstrate that a substantive architecture exists and can be stated clearly enough to be critiqued on its actual terms rather than reduced to its power budget. Why Power Accounting Is Necessary but Not Sufficient Any computational system intended to operate at stellar scale must first solve the problem of energy. At 1 AU the solar constant supplies a known flux; collector area and conversion efficiency determine available power; allocation to computation determines operations per second. These relations are engineering constraints, not explanations of intelligence. The Fraserphere treats stellar luminosity as the enabling substrate for a particular kind of computation — one that can be sustained for geological timescales without Earth-bound energy or cooling limits. Once that substrate is granted, the architectural questions become: what operations are performed with that power, how is state preserved and communicated across light-minute delays, and by what mechanism do those operations and communications produce coherent cognition rather than incoherent activity? The critique is therefore right to demand the latter answers. It is mistaken only in asserting that they have not been developed within the project. Node-Level Architecture: Memory, Operations, and Local Dynamics Each Fraserphere node is conceived as a photonic neuromorphic system rather than a general-purpose processor. Primitive operations are tensor contractions and convolutions implemented through programmable interferometer meshes or photonic crystal circuits. These are the same classes of operation that dominate modern neural network workloads, but executed at energies approaching 10−15 10^{-15} 10−15 J per primitive MAC or spiking event. In addition, the node supports local learning rules derived from predictive coding: each node continuously minimises a local variational free-energy functional. The gradients of this functional are realised through optical interference patterns and nonlinear optical elements rather than digital back-propagation. Memory is partitioned by timescale. Short-term state (current sensory predictions, recent prediction errors, and active inference roll-outs) resides in optical delay-line buffers whose length sets the temporal horizon of local prediction. Longer-term parameters (synaptic weights, priors over generative models) are stored in slower photonic or hybrid optoelectronic memory structures, refreshed on coordination-tier timescales. This separation mirrors the distinction between working memory and consolidated knowledge in biological systems and avoids the requirement for constant high-bandwidth refresh across the entire swarm. A single node therefore possesses both the computational primitives and the memory hierarchy required to run a local active inference loop at high speed. The 1.64×1017 1.64 \times 10^{17} 1.64×1017 ops/s figure characterises the throughput available to these loops, not an undifferentiated pool of generic operations. Interconnect, Latency, and Distributed State Light-time latency of approximately 17 minutes at 1 AU precludes any architecture that relies on tight global synchrony or low-latency gradient exchange. The Fraserphere interconnect model therefore does not attempt to eliminate latency; it treats latency as an observable that the system must model. Each node maintains a generative model that predicts both its local environment and the expected messages arriving from other nodes. Discrepancies between predicted and received messages constitute prediction error and drive updates to both the local model and (more slowly) the parameters that govern inter-node coordination. This is the standard active-inference solution to delayed and bandwidth-limited communication, scaled to stellar distances. A first-order link budget shows that wavelength-division multiplexed 1550 nm channels, combined with predictive buffering, can sustain coordination clusters of hundreds to thousands of nodes with aggregate data rates in the tens to hundreds of Gbps per node while keeping long-range traffic sparse. The architecture therefore contains an explicit interconnect strategy and an explicit mechanism for maintaining coherent distributed state despite propagation delay. The Mechanism Linking Operations to Cognition: Three-Tier NeuroSwarms The emergence of cognition is specified through a three-tier hierarchy rather than asserted as an automatic consequence of scale. Tier 1 (Local) — Photonic predictive-coding networks perform fast inference and learning within each node. These networks minimise local free energy and maintain high-resolution, short-horizon generative models of their immediate sensory and internal state. Tier 2 (Coordination) — Delay-compensated swarm metaheuristics (particle swarm optimisation augmented with predictive forward models, plus distributed but latency-aware gradient sharing) optimise routing, resource allocation, and local network topology. This tier operates on intermediate timescales and allows clusters of nodes to function as coherent sub-swarms. Tier 3 (Global) — Slow collective active inference aligns the generative models across the entire swarm. Evolutionary or meta-learning operators at this level permit the swarm to restructure its own connectivity patterns and learning rules over longer timescales. The global tier maintains a lower-resolution but spatially extended world model whose update cycle is set by light-time and coordination bandwidth rather than by any requirement for instantaneous consensus. Cognition, on this account, is the maintenance and refinement of a coherent generative model across scales and delays. Local operations supply the high-resolution, high-speed component; swarm-level rules supply the integrative, error-minimising dynamics that bind those local models into something larger. The leap from power to cognition is therefore not a single unsupported step but a sequence of explicit architectural commitments, each of which can be simulated or prototyped independently. Relation to the Simulation Hypothesis The Fraserphere was developed in parallel with explorations of the simulation hypothesis in which physical constants (notably c c c) function as computational limits, entanglement operates as a form of lazy global state resolution, and observers are embedded within a rendered substrate. In that framing, a stellar-scale photonic swarm is not merely an engineering project but a potential interface layer — a constructed system large enough and coherent enough to interact with the computational structure of the substrate itself at scales where local terrestrial computation cannot reach. This connection is not required for the architectural claims above, but it supplies additional motivation for why one would attempt to build coherent cognition at stellar rather than planetary scale. It also explains why latency is treated as a feature to be modelled rather than a bug to be eliminated: in a computational universe whose fundamental speed limit is c c c, any sufficiently large cognitive system must be delay-tolerant by design. Response to the Specific Critique The critique is correct on one point and mistaken on the central claim. It is correct that achieving numerical consistency between node count, collector area, and intercepted power is necessary but trivial compared with the problem of specifying a computational architecture. That correction was required housekeeping. It is mistaken in asserting that the Fraserphere framework supplies no memory model, no interconnect budget, no defined operations, and no mechanism linking operations to cognition. title: Research on Security Defense System for Tool-Augmented Agents
abstract: As LLM-driven tool-augmented agents deploy at scale, MCP and similar protocols expose unprecedented security attack surfaces. This paper analyzes security deficiencies in mainstream agent platforms, traces threat evolution from prompt injection through excessive agency to social engineering, and proposes a multi-layered defense architecture. Key contributions include revealing the "Master-Servant" architecture's inherent flaws, proposing a five-generation defense framework inspired by antivirus evolution, and building relational identity-based social engineering defense mechanisms. This work is part of the SIDOS framework.

title: ІНТЕЛЕКТУАЛЬНА СИСТЕМА УПРАВЛІННЯ ЦИФРОВИМИ МАРКЕТИНГОВИМИ КОМУНІКАЦІЯМИ НА ОСНОВІ ШТУЧНОГО ІНТЕЛЕКТУ ТА ЧАТ-БОТІВ
abstract: Topicality. The article substantiates a conceptual approach to optimizing and ensuring cybersecurity of digital communications management systems of enterprises by forming a single integrated information space of a business entity. The relevance of the study is due to the rapid deployment of artificial intelligence (AI), which has led to the emergence of specific cyber threats and risks of compromising confidential information at the points of infrastructure integration of linear MarTech platforms. The subject of the research is methods, models and tools for building an intelligent digital marketing communications management system based on artificial intelligence technologies, as well as mechanisms for ensuring its cybersecurity, verifying protection circuits and assessing the effectiveness of functioning in the context of the integration of digital MarTech platforms. The purpose of the article is to develop a conceptual model of an intelligent digital communications management system with verification of its security contours and the formation of an applied mathematical apparatus for assessing its effectiveness. The following results were obtained. A four-circuit architecture of the digital communications management system has been formed, where the basic digital infrastructure circuit acts as a source of primary data for the analytical AI core, and the security of access to CRM systems is regulated by a separate feedback loop. The information flows of the system have been formalized based on a set-theoretic approach using input parameters (set X) and output control signals (set Y), which record text and voice information protocols of dialogues. A model of integral evaluation of the system has been proposed, which consolidates operational-information, security and performance parameters. The results of calculating the eigenvector of the matrix using the T. Saati MAI (under the condition of full consistency, where VU = 0.69% < 10%) allowed us to determine the objective weighting factors of the system. It was found that the cybersecurity coefficient (γ = 0.297) and the level of automation of circuits (α = 0.163), which function in synergy with the productivity index (β = 0.540), are of great importance for ensuring the reliability of the architecture. Conclusion. The significance of the work lies in determining the strategic prospects for data protection through the deployment of a zero-trust architecture and AI governance standards, which protect personal data from unauthorized fine-tuning of public neural networks during operation.

title: Quantization-Jump SMOTE: Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique for Imbalanced Datasets with Discrete Quantized Levels
abstract: TClass imbalance is a pervasive challenge in data mining and machine learning, often leading classifiers to favor the majority class. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is widely used to address this issue by linearly interpolating between minority examples. However, standard SMOTE and its variants are primarily designed for continuous feature spaces. When applied to discrete, quantized, or ordinal features, continuous interpolation yields fractional values that violate the inherent physical constraints and structural rules of the data. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes Quantization-jump SMOTE (QJ-SMOTE), a novel over-sampling algorithm tailored for datasets with discrete quantized attributes. By incorporating predefined quantization steps and a discrete jump mechanism, QJ-SMOTE constrains the interpolation process to valid coordinate grids. Instead of using a continuous random factor, the algorithm introduces an integer-based jump factor that allows synthetic samples to land precisely on legitimate quantization levels. Theoretical analysis indicates that QJ-SMOTE effectively eliminates invalid "phantom samples" while generating valid, diverse synthetic data points. This approach successfully expands the decision boundaries of the minority class and enhances the generalization performance of classifiers on structurally restricted discrete datasets.

title: Research on Permutation-invariant SMOTE for Generating Synthetic Samples with Characteristic Permutation Invariance
abstract: The class imbalance problem is a critical bottleneck that severely limits the classification performance of machine learning models. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is widely used to mitigate this issue by interpolating new samples, it exhibits significant limitations when dealing with datasets that possess permutation invariance. Traditional SMOTE fails to account for the structural symmetry and ordering constraints among features, often generating "noisy" or invalid synthetic samples that violate the underlying physical or semantic rules of the data. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling framework named Permutation-invariant SMOTE (PI-SMOTE). The core idea of PI-SMOTE is to incorporate a permutation alignment mechanism into the neighborhood search and interpolation processes. Specifically, we define a permutation-invariant distance metric to locate true structural neighbors and derive an optimal alignment permutation matrix to map the nearest neighbor into the same topological space as the base sample. Linear interpolation is then performed within this aligned space, followed by a random permutation transformation to restore global structural diversity. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that PI-SMOTE effectively preserves the inherent permutation-invariant structure of the minority class without distorting its underlying data manifold. This method provides a rigorous and effective over-sampling solution for imbalanced learning tasks characterized by symmetric or permutation-invariant feature representations.

title: Selection Bias Correction in Retail Intelligence
abstract: Retail intelligence often relies on monitoring popular, high-velocity products, potentially biasing economic indicators by ignoring the "long tail" of niche items. This simulation study investigates selection bias in inflation estimation and compares correction methods across diverse data-generating processes. Through 400 Monte Carlo replications spanning four scenarios--aligned step functions, smooth gradients, misaligned breaks, and polynomial relationships--we test the robustness of Inverse Probability Weighting (IPW) with five specifications against stratification with varying strata counts. Our findings reveal fundamental limits of weighting methods in retail long-tail contexts: stratification achieves superior performance in three of four scenarios, maintaining sub-0.04pp median error even when boundaries deliberately misalign with population breaks (116x advantage over IPW). However, IPW with spline propensity models wins under smooth polynomial relationships (median error 0.007pp vs. 0.013pp), demonstrating context-dependency. Critically, even an oracle IPW specification with perfect structural knowledge achieves 6.06pp error compared to stratification's 0.008pp in step-function scenarios. This reflects violation of the Positivity Assumption--a fundamental causal inference requirement--rather than IPW methodological inferiority. When selection probabilities differ dramatically (90% vs. 1%), weighting methods operate outside their theoretical design envelope. These results demonstrate that stratification provides a safer engineering choice in retail long-tail distributions with severe positivity violations.

title: Triple-Phase Multimodal Knowledge Aggregation Framework for Microbial Keratitis Subtype Diagnosis on Slit-Lamp Photography
abstract: Microbial keratitis requires rapid pathogen identification to guide treatment, but culture- and PCR-based diagnostics are slow and resource-intensive. We developed a triple-phase multimodal framework for bacterial-versus-fungal keratitis classification using slit-lamp photographs acquired under blue-light, sclerotic-scatter, and white-light illumination, together with clinical metadata. The model combines cross-modality contrastive learning, modality-specific fine-tuning, and feature-level multimodal ensemble learning for patient-level prediction. We evaluated the framework on a multicenter dataset of 1,645 patients and 17,158 images from India and the United States. The model achieved 85.84% accuracy, 84.46% average F1-score, and 0.885 AUC. Site-specific evaluation showed that pooled results were overly optimistic, whereas resampling- and balance-based re-evaluation provided a more realistic assessment of cross-site generalization. Under all settings, our framework remained the top-performing approach. The code is available at https://github.com/yqwang01/TPMKA and dataset access will be provided subject to University of Michigan data-sharing clearance.

title: Resolución Cinemática de Paradojas Autorreferenciales en el Corpus IGLV
abstract: Este depósito presenta un modelo operativo para la resolución de paradojas autorreferenciales mediante la secuencia cinemática Dividir–Derivar–Trazar–Extrapolar, nativa del Corpus IGLV. El enfoque desplaza el problema desde la semántica del enunciado hacia la geometría informacional del anunciante, mostrando que la intratabilidad computacional asociada a bucles infinitos surge de la homogeneidad geométrica del sistema lógico tradicional. El modelo introduce la noción de curvatura informacional del nodo emisor y demuestra que, al fracturar topológicamente su identidad y proyectar su trayectoria más allá de la frontera crítica del sistema, la oscilación infinita se transforma en una operación discreta de clausura por inoperancia estructural. Este mecanismo se alinea con la Teoría de la Verdad Responsable (TVR 2.0) y el Principio G, proporcionando una vía geométrica para la neutralización de inestabilidades lógicas en arquitecturas de computación clásica y sistemas avanzados de IA. El depósito incluye el motor algorítmico completo en Python, validado empíricamente en entornos de ejecución estándar, que implementa las cuatro fases del proceso y permite reproducir los resultados de forma inmediata. Palabras clave: Corpus IGLV; paradojas autorreferenciales; topología de fronteras; complejidad computacional; TVR 2.0; Principio G; geometría informacional; Python.

title: Hybrid ABSA–C5.0 framework for interpretable classification of tourist perceptions in digital destination services
abstract: This study proposes an interpretable ABSA–C5.0 hybrid framework for analyzing tourists’ perceptions of digital destination information services. This framework integrates Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) for aspect extraction and sentiment assessment with C5.0 decision trees for classification and rule generation. This study follows the Knowledge Discovery in Databases (KDD) process, including preprocessing, feature engineering, modeling, and evaluation. The experiment uses a statistically synthesized dataset containing 72 labeled reviews, designed to reflect real-world online review patterns. With a 70:30 validation split, the model achieved 97.22% accuracy and a Cohen’s Kappa value of 0.947 in this controlled setting. However, these results are not intended for generalization, given the limited dataset size, synthetic data construction, and the absence of baseline comparisons and statistical significance tests. The extracted rules indicate that interactivity, clarity, and response speed are the primary factors driving positive perceptions. This framework is suitable for exploratory analysis, while further validation with real-world data and comparative models is required.

title: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF OPTIMIZATION ALGORITHMS AND MIXED-PRECISION TRAINING FOR MINIMIZING NEURAL NETWORK TRAINING TIME
abstract: Topicality. The rapid growth of deep learning applications has placed training time among the most critical engineering constraints in neural network development. Modern architectures such as ResNet-18 and MobileNetV2 require substantial computational resources even for compact benchmarks, making training efficiency a pressing problem for researchers with limited hardware budgets. The subject of study is the combined effect of three first-order optimization algorithms — SGD with momentum, Adam, and AdamW – together with automatic mixed-precision (FP16/FP32) arithmetic on per-epoch training time, GPU memory consumption, and classification accuracy. The purpose of the article is to quantify and compare six optimizers × precision configurations on a consumer-grade GPU to identify the combination that minimizes training time subject to a 1 % accuracy tolerance. The following results were obtained. Experiments on an NVIDIA RTX 3060 Ti with ResNet-18 and MobileNetV2 trained on CIFAR-10 for 100 epochs showed that AdamW with PyTorch AMP reduced per-epoch training time by 29–31 % relative to SGD FP32 while improving validation accuracy by 1.5–2.5 percentage points. Peak GPU memory decreased by approximately 30 % under AMP. Conclusion. Decoupled weight decay combined with half-precision tensor arithmetic is an effective strategy for minimizing neural network training time on modern consumer GPUs. The results provide a reproducible benchmark and motivate further research into adaptive optimizer switching and cross-platform energy-efficiency metrics.

title: Reward Lightning: Fast Video Generation via Homologous Preference Distillation
abstract: Achieving simultaneous preference alignment and distillation acceleration in video diffusion models remains an open challenge. Existing methods optimize the two objectives over mismatched representation spaces, where improving one objective often compromises the other. To overcome this, we propose Reward Lightning, a unified framework that aligns and accelerates a video diffusion model within a single shared representation. Its central principle is homology: both objectives are evaluated on identical latent features, which mitigates the gradient conflicts that arise when they are optimized over disjoint representations. As a foundational component, we first introduce a latent reward model (LRM) that scores videos directly in the latent space, without decoding back to the pixel space. Building on the LRM, homologous preference distillation (HPD) reuses this shared backbone to perform adversarial distillation and preference alignment jointly, yielding few-step generators that remain faithful and well aligned. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the LRM surpasses pixel-level and latent-level reward baselines by $11.0\%$ and $14.7\%$ in preference accuracy, and that Reward Lightning generates high-fidelity videos in merely $1$ to $4$ steps, improving the average VBench score by $2.1\%$ while leading in text alignment, motion quality, and visual quality. Project page: https://reward-lightning.github.io.

title: Synthesizing Minority Samples via Feature Narration Logic for Imbalanced Classification
abstract: In the field of machine learning and data mining, class imbalance presents a major challenge as standard classifiers tend to favor the majority class, leading to poor recognition of the minority class. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and its variants are widely used to address this issue, they predominantly rely on linear interpolation based on Euclidean distance in the feature space. This mathematical approximation often overlooks the intrinsic logical relationships and joint synergies among features, leading to the creation of "phantom samples" that contradict real-world domain logic and introduce noise into the training set. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling methodology named Feature Narration SMOTE (FN-SMOTE). The core concept of FN-SMOTE is to treat the feature sequence of a sample as an organized "narration structure", where the progression of feature values represents the development of a logical storyline. By leveraging a first-order Markov chain assumption, the method constructs a feature narration chain along with conditional probability transition matrices from the minority class distribution. During the sample generation process, an initial candidate sample generated by traditional interpolation undergoes a step-by-step correction mechanism to ensure each feature adheres to the conditional probability constraints. Finally, a global Narration Deviation (ND) metric is applied to filter out logically inconsistent samples. This approach shifts the paradigm of over-sampling from pure spatial proximity to structural and logical plausibility, effectively synthesizing high-quality minority samples that are both statistically representative and logically sound for downstream classification tasks.

title: IMPLEMENTATION AND EVALUATION OF A QUANTUM RANDOM NUMBER GENERATOR BASED ON ANU QRNG FOR CRYPTOGRAPHIC APPLICATION
abstract: Topicality. Reliable random number generation is one of the key requirements for modern cryptographic systems and cybersecurity applications. Traditional pseudo-random number generators are based on deterministic algorithms and may exhibit limited entropy and predictability, which can negatively affect information security. The subject of study in the article is methods of quantum random number generation and approaches to evaluating the quality of generated random sequences. The purpose of the article is to analyze modern methods of quantum random number generation, develop a software tool for obtaining quantum random numbers based on the ANU Quantum Random Number Generator service, perform statistical testing of the generated sequences, and analyze the obtained results. The following results were obtained. Modern quantum random number generation systems were analyzed and compared. A software tool was implemented in Python for automatic retrieval of quantum random numbers through the ANU QRNG API. The generated binary sequences were evaluated using Frequency Test and Block Frequency Test from the NIST SP 800-22 statistical test suite. The obtained p-values were 0.977181 and 0.200659 respectively, confirming successful completion of both tests. Additionally, visual analysis of the generated sequences revealed no noticeable patterns or repetitive structures. Conclusion. The obtained results confirm the high quality of quantum random sequences generated using ANU QRNG and demonstrate the applicability of the developed software tool for cryptographic and cybersecurity applications requiring high-quality randomness.

title: Cross-Modal Fusion of OCT and OCT angiography enface for Improved Diagnostics of Diabetic Retinopathy
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of vision impairment worldwide, highlighting the need for accurate and accessible screening tools. Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) provides high-resolution structural information of the retina, whereas OCT angiography (OCTA) offers complementary vascular information that is highly relevant for DR diagnosis. In this study, we propose a cross-modal fusion of OCT B-scans with single-channel en face OCTA using a bidirectional cross-modal attention network for automated DR classification. Two independent datasets, OCT500 and UIC, comprising 730 subjects in total, were utilized to evaluate performance under within-dataset, combined-dataset, and cross-dataset generalization settings. A ConvNeXt V2 model trained solely on OCT images served as the unimodal baseline. In addition to ground-truth (GT) OCTA, we explored the use of translated (TR) OCTA generated from OCT scans, eliminating the requirement for dedicated OCTA hardware. Experimental results demonstrate that cross-modal fusion consistently outperforms unimodal OCT classification across all evaluation scenarios. Fusion with GT OCTA improved classification accuracy and discriminative performance, while TR OCTA achieved comparable or superior results in most settings. Furthermore, TR OCTA improved sensitivity and cross-dataset generalization, indicating enhanced robustness to domain shifts. These findings demonstrate that attention-based OCT-OCTA en face fusion provides clinically meaningful improvements for DR detection and suggest that computationally generated OCTA can serve as a practical, low-cost alternative to hardware-acquired OCTA, enabling broader deployment of high-performance retinal screening systems in resource-limited clinical environments.

title: The Covariant N-Max Framework: Riemannian Geometry and the Asymmetric Knuth–Moore Isomorphism—Experimental Code
abstract: This repository contains the standalone C++ algorithmic suite, tournament framework, and raw empirical data logs supporting the publication: "The Covariant N-Max Framework: Riemannian Geometry and the Asymmetric Knuth-Moore Isomorphism" (DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20956411). The codebase empirically validates the theoretical projections of the Covariant N-Max framework by executing a multi-threaded 3-player Hexagonal Chess (Hexchess3) tournament suite. It demonstrates the kinematic evolution of algorithms operating across different mathematical topologies, from the unconstrained classical baseline (max^N) and the static Euclidean zero-sum baseline (N-Max) to the dynamic Riemannian algorithm (Covariant Hypermax). Archive Contents: - C++ Algorithmic Engines: 6 standalone structural variations representing the heuristic search algorithms evaluated in the empirical tournaments. - Orchestrator Programs: Multi-threaded C++ orchestrators (D4.cpp, D5.cpp, D6.cpp) designed to execute parallel tournament phases across all seating permutations. - - Raw Empirical Data: Complete, unedited CSV logs representing 7,560 games across 18 tournament blocks, validating the algorithmic pruning factors and win distributions presented in Table 1 of the manuscript. - Visualizer Demo: A lightweight, TrueColor console application (Demo_HexChess3_3xCovHX_D6.cpp) that allows reviewers to visually observe the Covariant Hypermax algorithm rendering and playing a live game at d=6.

title: Parallel Dimensional Core Learning: A Library-Free Graph-Based Multidimensional Deep Learning Architecture with Compiler-Style Parallel Training, Adaptive Pruning and Graph-Weighted Gradient Aggregation
abstract: I present Parallel Dimensional Core Learning (PDCL), a graph-based multidimensional deep learning architecture built entirely from raw matrix operations without any deep learning framework dependencies. PDCL is not a transformer — it is a fundamentally different architecture that replaces monolithic sequential processing with parallel dimensional computation, graph-weighted gradient aggregation, and adaptive pruning. PDCL introduces five interconnected mechanisms that collectively address fundamental limitations of standard deep learning architectures

title: KC-SMOTE: Knowledge-Constraint Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique for Imbalanced Data Classification
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in machine learning and data mining applications. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is widely used to address this issue by linearly interpolating between minority class samples. However, standard SMOTE purely relies on geometric distances in the feature space, inherently ignoring the underlying logical relations and domain knowledge behind the data. This blindness often leads to the generation of "noisy" or unrealizable virtual samples that violate real-world rules, thereby degrading the generalizability of downstream classifiers. To resolve this limitation, this paper proposes an improved over-sampling framework named Knowledge-constraint SMOTE (KC-SMOTE). The core idea is to introduce an external Knowledge Graph (KG) to guide and constrain the synthetic sample generation process. Specifically, logical rules and domain boundaries are extracted from the KG and transformed into multivariate inequalities and logical determinants within the feature space. During the interpolation process, a "validation-correction-elimination" mechanism is implemented to evaluate the synthetic instances. Samples that violate the knowledge constraints are either projected onto the nearest compliant boundaries or discarded. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that KC-SMOTE effectively eliminates logically contradictory samples and shapes a more precise decision boundary that aligns with the true latent manifold of the data. This knowledge-driven approach significantly enhances both the semantic plausibility of generated samples and the robustness of the resulting classification models.

title: Comparative performance of IndoBERT-based deep learning models with SMOTE for trade tariff sentiment analysis
abstract: The rapid growth of social media discussions on trade tariff policies has produced large volumes of Indonesian-language opinion data, making sentiment analysis an important tool for understanding public responses. However, studies in this domain remained limited, particularly those addressing class imbalance and comparing multiple hybrid architectures. This study aimed to compare four IndoBERT-based model configurations, with and without the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), for classifying sentiment in Indonesian trade tariff discussions under class imbalance. The dataset consisted of Indonesian tweets related to trade tariffs collected from X (Twitter) between January and July 2025. The configurations were Logistic Regression as a baseline, IndoBERT-BiLSTM, IndoBERT-CNN, and IndoBERT-BiLSTM-CNN. The tweets were passed through IndoBERT to generate contextual embeddings without fine-tuning. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and macro F1-score, with macro F1-score as the primary metric. The results showed that IndoBERT-CNN with SMOTE achieved the best macro F1-score of 0.7657 and an accuracy of 0.8654. SMOTE consistently improved recall across all deep learning architectures, with IndoBERT-CNN gaining the most, from 0.7304 to 0.7875. These findings showed that, among the four compared configurations, IndoBERT-CNN with SMOTE provided the most balanced performance for imbalanced Indonesian trade tariff sentiment classification.

title: Performance Analysis of Deep Learning Algorithms for Journal Classification
abstract: The expansion of biomedical literature available in online databases has created significant hurdles for researchers trying to find relevant resources using standard keyword searches. With the rapid increase in web-based medical research, there's a growing demand for smart and precise extraction methods that can sift through vast biomedical databases to identify the most useful literature. The National Centre for Biotechnology Information (NCBI)’s PubMed is a vital source of peer-reviewed biomedical research articles. This repository is highly used by researchers and healthcare practitioners for their research purpose. In this study, the dataset is manually downloaded from the PubMed Database and the performance of various deep learning algorithms, such as K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), in classifying biomedical texts is analysed. Techniques based on deep learning provide a powerful end-to-end solution for accurate label classification.

title: VFA: Empowering Multilingual MLLMs via Vision-Free Adaptation
abstract: Multimodal large language models have advanced rapidly, yet most remain English-centric, as scaling multilingual multimodal instruction tuning is limited by the scarcity and high cost of high-quality non-English image-text supervision. Although multilingual text data is abundant, naive textual fine-tuning can disrupt vision-language alignment and induce catastrophic forgetting. We propose Vision-Free Adaptation (VFA), a framework that decouples multilingual language enhancement from visual alignment by composing complementary task vectors over a shared LLM backbone. Specifically, we fine-tune a base LLM on multilingual text data to derive a multilingual task vector, which is then merged with the vision-aligned task vector of an MLLM. Experiments on five MLLMs across six multilingual multimodal benchmarks show consistent improvements while preserving both general multimodal and text-only capabilities. Moreover, using less than 2% of the text data, VFA narrows the gap to the fully multimodal-trained model, demonstrating its data efficiency.

title: WSA_1: a 3D-Centric World-Spatial-Action Model for Generalizable Robot Control
abstract: Recent advances in embodied AI have established robot foundation models (RFMs) as the dominant approach for generalist robotic systems to date. By leveraging imitation learning on extensive robot demonstrations, RFMs have achieved impressive capabilities in mapping visual observations and language instructions to continuous robotic actions. However, current RFMs lack an inherent ability to reason about physical dynamics and the causal effects of robot behaviors on the 3D physical world. This creates a fundamental mismatch between 2D-centric visual perception and 3D-centric embodied interaction, severely limiting the generalization ability of RFMs in real-world tasks.To address this gap, we present WSA_1, a novel RFM built upon proposed 3D-Centric World-Spatial-Action modeling paradigm. It not only learns 3D world-aware visual thought for future robot behaviors, but also models mutual constraints between 3D world state transitions and robotic actions to enhance behavior generalization. Notably, WSA_1 achieves highly data-efficient pre-training with 6k hours of expert demonstration data (only 1k hours from real robot), while delivering competitive manipulation performance (93% success rate) on RoboTwin2.0 simulation benchmark and achieving +20% average boosted performance over state-of-the-art RFMs on real-world robot control tasks. These results reveal that generalizable RFM can be attained without large-scale real robot data when paired with 3D-centric world-action joint modeling, which offers a practical and affordable pathway to generalist robotic systems.

title: LLM-Free Semantic Graph Preprocessing for Scalable AI Architectures
abstract: This research paper evaluates an architectural shift in large-scale artificial intelligence applications, moving away from generative-dependent data ingestion toward local, embedding-based semantic graph construction. Adapting the LiteSemRAG framework, the document outlines a preprocessing pipeline designed to significantly reduce computational overhead, token consumption, and network latency. The proposed decoupled system delegates structural data mapping to lightweight local models, optimizing performance for automated evaluation systems, real-time virtual environments, and asynchronous community discussion platforms.

title: Similarity Inversion SMOTE: A Novel Over-Sampling Strategy Specifically Executing Far-Sighted Minority Sample Generation
abstract: In imbalanced data classification, Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and its various extensions conventionally adhere to the "neighborhood similarity" principle, which synthesizes new instances by interpolating between closely situated minority samples. However, this traditional "near-to-near" generation mechanism frequently triggers overfitting and exacerbates the fuzziness of overlapping decision regions. To break through this inherent limitation, this paper proposes a brand-new over-sampling strategy named Similarity Inversion SMOTE (SI-SMOTE). The core idea of this algorithm is to deliberately generate synthetic samples under a "similarity inversion rule", thereby constructing a novel "near-to-far" spatial topology. This mechanism guides new instances to extend toward distant regions where the minority class possesses weaker control but high potential classification value. We detail the mathematical formulation and algorithmic pipeline of SI-SMOTE, and theoretically validate its effectiveness from the perspectives of topological boundary expansion and generalization enhancement. This work offers a counter-intuitive yet highly effective perspective on data augmentation for imbalanced learning tasks.

title: Multi-source Teacher-Student Learning for Cross-Lingual NER with LLM Fine-Tuning
abstract: To better tackle the named entity recognition (NER) problem on languages with little/no labeled data, cross-lingual NER must effectively leverage knowledge learned from source languages with rich labeled data. However, such methods either are not applicable if the labeled data in the source languages is unavailable, or do not leverage information contained in unlabeled data in the target language. title: A Reliability-Aware Landsat Framework for Sustainable Geothermal Resource Potential Assessment: A Case Study from Quzhou, Eastern China
abstract: Thermal infrared land-surface temperature (LST) anomalies can support early-stage geothermal reconnaissance, but in humid, vegetated and urbanizing low-temperature regions they are readily affected by land cover, terrain and human activity. This study develops a reliability-aware Landsat 8 framework for Quzhou, eastern China. Landsat 8 Collection 2 winter scenes from 2016 to 2025 were cloud-screened, converted to LST, and composited using a per-pixel median strategy. NDVI, NDBI and NDWI masks reduced vegetation, impervious-surface and water interference. Standardized LST anomalies were integrated with a 3 km local-relief constraint, candidate-patch vectorization, and patch-level scoring based on thermal persistence, terrain context, land-cover reliability, structural proximity and lithology/contact favorability. General and strong winter LST anomalies cover approximately 64.4 and 22.3 km2, respectively, with impervious surfaces accounting for 55.97% and 67.65% before reliability screening. The terrain-constrained workflow reduces the candidate area to approximately 22.2 km2 and ranks 267 patches, including 27 very-high relative reconnaissance-priority patches. The highest-ranked patches are characterized mainly by combined thermal persistence, lower land-cover interference, favorable fault proximity and favorable lithology/contact settings, indicating relative priority rather than confirmed resources. Integrated reliability screening is therefore essential before using Landsat LST anomalies for geothermal target prioritization.

title: Метод блокчейн-консенсусной распределенной классификации изображений
abstract: Предметом исследования являются методы межузловой агрегации обновлений и локальных визуальных представлений в распределенных системах классификации изображений. Цель работы состоит в разработке и экспериментальной проверке метода блокчейн-консенсусной распределенной классификации изображений, ориентированного на повышение устойчивости глобальной модели в условиях неоднородных, шумных и частично вредоносных источников данных. Предлагаемый подход сочетает локальные классовые атласы признаков, аудит-проверку полезности клиентских обновлений, робастную оценку аномальности локальных траекторий и блокчейн-фиксируемое консенсусное взвешивание вклада узлов. Для экспериментальной проверки использованы открытые наборы изображений CIFAR-10 и Olivetti Faces, а сравнение выполнено в сценариях iid_clean, noniid_clean, noniid_noisy и noniid_adversarial. title: Position: AI Leaderboards Are Underserving the Global South: A Case Study from India
abstract: This position paper argues that AI leaderboards are structurally ill-suited to serving the Global South because they lack independent governance, conflict-of-interest policies, and mechanisms for metric evolution. The barrier is not missing data; high-quality regional benchmarks already exist: IndicSUPERB, MILU, and LAHAJA for India; IrokoBench for Africa; AlGhafa for Arabic. The barrier is institutional design. Global leaderboards do not include these benchmarks, and no governance mechanism compels them to do so. Commercial pressure corrects leaderboard failures when paying customers in the Global North are affected. The Global South lacks equivalent leverage. Without governance, failures affecting Hindi, Swahili, or Arabic speakers persist indefinitely as documented but unaddressed gaps. Using India as a case study (1.4 billion people, 22 scheduled languages, high-quality benchmarks, but no trusted aggregation), we report findings from a consultation with 58 AI practitioners showing consistent preference for formal governance and disclosure-based conflict management. The solution is not more data but better institutions: regional leaderboards with independent governance from the start.

title: ProxyUp: Training-Free Proxy-Conditioned Video Generation for Controllable Dynamics
abstract: Precise control over complex dynamics remains challenging for modern video generative models, as text prompts alone often cannot specify physically plausible, fine-grained motion and interactions. We introduce $\textit{proxy-conditioned video generation}$, where a coarse proxy video from physics-based simulation or real-world recording serves as a dynamics carrier to control foreground object motion. Given a proxy video and a text prompt, the goal is to synthesize a new video that preserves the proxy dynamics while generating novel content and plausible interactions aligned with the prompt. Since paired proxy-target videos are difficult to obtain, we propose $\textbf{ProxyUp}$, a training-free framework built on pretrained video generative models. ProxyUp first inverts the proxy video into an intermediate latent representation and applies $\textbf{region-wise latent noising}$, preserving motion-critical proxy latents while injecting noise into regions intended for text-driven regeneration. To mitigate the distribution mismatch and weak foreground-background coupling introduced by this heuristic latent composition, we further propose $\textbf{Stochastic Flow Relaxation (SFR)}$, which progressively relaxes the composed latent toward the model's learned distribution before ODE sampling. Experiments on both simulation and real-world proxies show that ProxyUp outperforms strong video editing and motion transfer baselines in dynamic fidelity and text alignment.

title: Efficient Authenticated Fine-Grained Access Engine for Encrypted Data in Mobile Edge Cloud
abstract: Fine-grained, authenticated, traceable, and efficient encrypted access control is indispensable for secure data sharing in mobile edge cloud networks, especially for resource-constrained data requesters. Despite the prevalence of outsourced ciphertext-policy attribute-based encryption (CP-ABE) solutions, existing schemes still suffer from critical practical limitations. First, requester-side transformation keys are typically unverified prior to computationally expensive outsourced decryption operations. Second, commitment-based verification mechanisms fail to validate the identity of data publishers. Third, the online computational overhead scales linearly with either the requester attribute set or the policy-matching set, severely degrading practical efficiency. To address these issues, this paper proposes ePoFSC, a novel policy-oriented functional signcryption scheme for authenticated encrypted data sharing in mobile edge cloud scenarios. The proposed ePoFSC scheme integrates pre-auditing and caching mechanisms for requester trapdoors before online access requests, enabling constant-time operations for request generation, request verification, and request header construction independent of requester attribute scale. In the outsourced decryption phase, ePoFSC offloads all costly pairing and exponentiation operations with constant computational complexity, leaving only lightweight policy-dependent group multiplications for terminal requesters. Furthermore, ePoFSC tightly couples decryption verification with publisher authentication and requester traceability to realize comprehensive access accountability. Rigorous security analysis formally validates the confidentiality, publisher-side unforgeability, and requester traceability of the proposed scheme. Extensive experimental evaluations on the BLS12-381 curve verify that ePoFSC achieves prominent performance superiority over existing state-of-the-art schemes in both the encryption and data recovery phases.

title: CoGen3D: An Agentic Human-AI Co-Design Pipeline for 3D Asset Generation for Virtual Reality
abstract: Creating 3D assets for virtual reality requires modeling expertise, which restricts the authorship of immersive experiences. Existing generative AI tools rely on unconstrained, command-driven prompting, lacking the conversational scaffolding needed for users to articulate their intent and validate designs prior to rendering. To address this, we introduce CoGen3D, an agentic human-AI co-design pipeline that proactively guides users through conversational intent elicitation, a concept image confirmation, and image-to-3D generation that directly deploys to immersive scenes. We evaluated this system through a user study (N=120) across six affectively diverse immersive scenes, observing 60 Design group participants who co-created 3D assets for the scenes, and 60 Validation group participants who experienced the scenes with generated assets. Our findings show that co-designed assets are associated with higher scene engagement and shifted affective responses, while participants generally preferred concept images over the final 3D assets, with no increased leniency toward degradation in their own creations. Analysis of the human-AI conversations further shows that target environments shape users' conversational patterns. Our results suggest that our staged, intent-based co-design can democratize virtual reality authoring and shift immersive content creation from technical execution toward collaborative spatial design.

title: Research on Unbalanced Data SMOTE Algorithm Based on Micro-state Variable Set Expansion
abstract: Class imbalance classification is a prevailing and challenging issue in the fields of machine learning and data mining. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is widely used to address this problem, traditional SMOTE and its variants operate strictly at the "sample level" by executing linear interpolations in the macro feature space. This sample-level paradigm inherently suffers from decision boundary blurring, over-generalization, and a lack of physical or logical constraints, which frequently leads to the generation of implausible or counter-factual samples. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling methodology named Micro-state Expansion SMOTE (ME-SMOTE). Departing from traditional sample-space manipulation, ME-SMOTE introduces the micro-state theory from statistical physics to deconstruct macro data samples into underlying, dynamic micro-state variable sets via a mathematical deconstruction operator. Within the hidden micro-state space, instead of linear interpolation, the algorithm executes state-level non-linear selection, crossover, and recombination governed by transition affinity matrix and state position controllers, effectively simulating the microscopic thermal fluctuations of the data-generating system. Subsequently, a reconstruction operator maps the expanded micro-state sets back into the macro feature space. To guarantee the real-world physical validity and classification effectiveness of the synthesized data, a dual-layer validation mechanism consisting of micro-state compatibility constraints and a macro compliance filter is established to eliminate invalid state combinations and prevent sample invasion into majority class territories. Theoretical analysis indicates that ME-SMOTE successfully uncovers latent, unobserved yet physically consistent state combinations, significantly enriching the diversity of the minority class while maintaining sharp and meaningful decision boundaries. This framework provides an interpretable and mechanism-driven perspective for handling highly imbalanced datasets in complex systems.

title: Blockchain-Driven Federated Learning for Secure Industrial Predictive Maintenance
abstract: Factories with similar machines could build better failure-prediction models by sharing data, but most do not want to share their raw records with competitors or a central server. Federated learning (FL) solves this problem by allowing each factory to keep its data locally while training a shared model. However, FL still depends on a central server and does not clearly track contributions. This paper shows a framework that combines FL with a lightweight permissioned ledger. Each factory trains a local model, signs its update, and stores only a hash of the update on the ledger. This provides data integrity, an audit trail, and controlled participation. Using the AI4I 2020 predictive-maintenance dataset across five simulated factories, the framework achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.949, close to the centralized model’s 0.974 and much better than a single factory’s 0.790. The ledger added only about 6% extra training time and required very little storage. This helps identify and remove malicious participants, making industrial data sharing more secure and trustworthy.

title: "Submarine Terminator Trained by Reinforcement Learning"
abstract: " Which statistic should a study of adversarial reinforcement learning (RL) report: the average score of a training run, or the probability that a run produces a deployable policy at all? We argue for the latter \u2014 the training yield \u2014 in a three-dimensional submarine return-to-base game in which autonomous naval mines learn to intercept a Deep Q-Network (DQN) navigator that completes 100% of missions against scripted mines. Thirty-six replicates of one fixed mine recipe, differing only in training seed, produce a zero-inflated and wide outcome distribution: eleven runs never learn, and the rest spread from 19% to 98% held-out kill rate. The average-score view calls the recipe mediocre (mean 34.4% \u00b1 35.5, median 26.5%); the yield view says it manufactures a \u226590% \"Terminator\" adversary in 11.1% of runs (Wilson 95% CI [4.4, 25.3]), at roughly 50k episodes of expected compute per success, provided both the final weights and the best training-time snapshot are evaluated on held-out seeds.That proviso is the paper's second theme: every training-time metric we examined was inflated by evaluation artifacts. An \"improved\" mine agent combining five standard refinements logs a 57.7% kill rate over its final training episodes yet kills nothing under greedy held-out evaluation (0%, CI [0, 1.3]); because the training script seeds the global RNG per episode, we decompose that gap, without approximation, into curriculum, opponent-pool, and exploration components. The plausible causal story \u2014 that an entropy regularizer destroyed the policy \u2014 fails two audits: the raw entropy\u2013lethality correlation (r = \u22120.20) vanishes under schedule controls (r = \u22120.02), and a single-variable sweep finds no destructive entropy effect. Best-snapshot selection on the training metric reproduces the deployed agent's 98% headline from a 69.7% run. Training yield under honest held-out selection turns seed variance from a reproducibility hazard into a costed optimization resource; training-time metrics, single-run causal attributions, and single-run policy characterizations support none of the claims built on them."

evidence.title: "Submarine Terminator Trained by Reinforcement Learning"
evidence.abstract: " Which statistic should a study of adversarial reinforcement learning (RL) report: the average score of a training run, or the probability that a run produces a deployable policy at all? We argue for the latter \u2014 the training yield \u2014 in a three-dimensional submarine return-to-base game in which autonomous naval mines learn to intercept a Deep Q-Network (DQN) navigator that completes 100% of missions against scripted mines. Thirty-six replicates of one fixed mine recipe, differing only in training seed, produce a zero-inflated and wide outcome distribution: eleven runs never learn, and the rest spread from 19% to 98% held-out kill rate. The average-score view calls the recipe mediocre (mean 34.4% \u00b1 35.5, median 26.5%); the yield view says it manufactures a \u226590% \"Terminator\" adversary in 11.1% of runs (Wilson 95% CI [4.4, 25.3]), at roughly 50k episodes of expected compute per success, provided both the final weights and the best training-time snapshot are evaluated on held-out seeds.That proviso is the paper's second theme: every training-time metric we examined was inflated by evaluation artifacts. An \"improved\" mine agent combining five standard refinements logs a 57.7% kill rate over its final training episodes yet kills nothing under greedy held-out evaluation (0%, CI [0, 1.3]); because the training script seeds the global RNG per episode, we decompose that gap, without approximation, into curriculum, opponent-pool, and exploration components. The plausible causal story \u2014 that an entropy regularizer destroyed the policy \u2014 fails two audits: the raw entropy\u2013lethality correlation (r = \u22120.20) vanishes under schedule controls (r = \u22120.02), and a single-variable sweep finds no destructive entropy effect. Best-snapshot selection on the training metric reproduces the deployed agent's 98% headline from a 69.7% run. Training yield under honest held-out selection turns seed variance from a reproducibility hazard into a costed optimization resource; training-time metrics, single-run causal attributions, and single-run policy characterizations support none of the claims built on them."

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare: Developing Trustworthy Predictive Models for Clinical Decision Support Systems
abstract: Explainable AI can enhance clinical decision support, providing not just prediction but also clarity. In this study, a framework for explainable predictive modelling for spine related diagnostic classification was developed and evaluated. A secondary dataset of 310 patients with six biomechanical features of the spine was used to categorize patients into Disk Hernia, Normal and Spondylolisthesis. Eight supervised machine learning models were tested. The accuracy, macro F1 score, weighted F1 score, receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration assessment, cross validation, error analysis and SHAP-based explainability were used to assess the final model. Gradient Boosting had the best performance with test accuracy 0.8387, macro F1-score 0.7711, weighted F1-score 0.8332, macro receiver operating characteristic area 0.9204, and weighted receiver operating characteristic area 0.9389. Spondylolisthesis showed the best discrimination from Normal cases and Disk Hernia showed less discrimination. The most significant explanatory features identified by SHAP analysis were degree of spondylolisthesis, sacral slope and pelvic radius. The proposed framework showed that explainable AI could be used to enable transparent clinical decision support in the field of spine. The model should be seen, however, as an assistive system proof of concept that needs to be further validated.

title: Human In the Loop Challenges for Quality Annotation of Pre-Cancer Lesions in Clinical Oral Images
abstract: Abstract Smartphone-based Artificial Intelligence (AI) enabled screening of the hyperplasia and dysplasia stages (pre-cancer, OPMD) offers a viable opportunity to reduce the incidence and mortality of oral cancer through early prevention. However, developing accurate segmentation models requires high-quality, pixel-level annotations that are prohibitively expensive and prone to clinical subjectivity. To address this, we empirically validated a deep learning-driven Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) iterative pseudo-labeling framework to pixel-annotate 3,026 clinical oral images. We also conducted controlled experiments to quantify the network’s tolerance to label noise (unreviewed pseudo-labels) and resolved clinical subjectivity using pixel-wise Cohen’s Kappa and the STAPLE consensus algorithm. While iterative self-training consistently improved lesion detection and spatial localization, including even a modest fraction ( → 10%) of unreviewed pseudo-labels increased training convergence instability three-to-four-fold and induced a conservative prediction bias that negatively impacted model recall. Ultimately, the model’s performance converged with the inter-rater reliability ceiling ( κ → 0.65) against a multi-expert ground truth, successfully falling within the envelope of human agreement. These findings highlight that non-experts can successfully drive the early-to-mid stages of the annotation pipeline, but a final expert-driven quality assurance step is strictly essential to mitigate training instability, confirmation bias, and clinically unacceptable recall drops. Overall, this provides a scalable, empirically validated blueprint for building domain-specific medical imaging datasets in global health settings where annotation cost, inter-observer variability, and expert unavailability challenges are most acute.

title: Domain-Specific Fine-Tuning in Multimodal Cross-Lingual NER for Low-Resource Languages
abstract: Cross-lingual Named Entity Recognition (NER) leverages knowledge transfer between languages to identify and classify named entities, making it particularly useful for low-resource languages. We show that the data-based cross-lingual transfer method is an effective technique for crosslingual NER and can outperform multilingual language models for low-resource languages. title: A Large-Scale Crowdsourced Sinhala Narrative Corpus for Low-Resource NLP: The sinhala_stories Dataset
abstract: sinhala_stories is a crowdsourced corpus of Sinhala-language narrative text comprising 10,949,007 rows (~2.09 GB) in Apache Parquet format, collected through a public Streamlit submission portal integrated with the Hugging Face Hub. Each submission was validated for Sinhala script content, length, language-identification confidence, and heuristic spam/duplicate checks before being merged into the corpus via an automated CI/CD pipeline. Content warning: a substantial portion of the corpus consists of explicit adult narrative content, submitted with minimal moderation beyond character-level validation. Anyone training generative models on this data should apply content filtering and safety alignment before deployment. See the accompanying data note for full ethical considerations. Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Isuru0x01/sinhala_storiesCollection app source: https://github.com/isuru0x01/Sinhala-Stories-Dataset-Creator

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Adversarial Attacks and Defense Strategies in Artificial Intelligence Security
abstract: The growing deployment of deep learning models in safety-critical domains has exposed the artificial intelligence landscape to a widening array of adversarial threats, where imperceptible input perturbations reliably induce severe misclassifications. This survey provides a comprehensive synthesis of adversarial attacks and defense mechanisms in modern AI security. It introduces a structured taxonomy categorizing attacks into evasion, poisoning, and model inversion strategies, evaluated across varying levels of attacker knowledge. Correspondingly, current defense techniques—including adversarial training, anomaly detection, and gradient masking—are critically reviewed for their resilience against adaptive, real-world adversaries. The survey further examines robustness benchmarking and success rate analysis frameworks, emphasizing the gap between theoretical guarantees and practical deployment. By consolidating recent advances and persistent limitations, this work identifies open research challenges and outlines emerging directions toward provably secure and trustworthy AI systems for real-world applications.

title: xuzhougeng/wisp-science: v0.4.1
abstract: <!-- release-title: v1.10.0: MCP --> wisp-science v1.10.0 v1.10.0 brings scientific MCP tools into Wisp's native Rust runtime. The bundled catalog provides 23 connectors and 247 tools across roughly 80 upstream databases, with browsable connector introductions and tool parameters. This release also improves first-time setup, settings navigation, and Python/R skill execution. Downloads macOS (.dmg, signed + notarized): Apple Silicon (aarch64) and Intel (x86_64); compatible versions can update in-app. Windows (MSI / NSIS): installers remain unsigned while SignPath release signing is disabled. Windows may show SmartScreen; review the publisher details before proceeding. Linux (deb / AppImage): x86_64 and aarch64. Installers are attached to Assets as the platform builds finish. Highlights Native Scientific MCP Desktop, CLI, and the ACP bridge share the Rust wisp-bio catalog. Bundled scientific retrieval no longer launches the vendored Python MCP servers; Python is still available for analysis and custom MCP services that need it. The catalog covers literature, omics archives, genes and ontologies, variants, proteins, structures, chemistry, clinical trials, and research resources. Sources include PubMed, GEO, UniProt, ChEMBL, OpenAlex, arXiv, bioRxiv/medRxiv, and ZINC. Native coverage includes KEGG, CADD, PanglaoDB, and Sanger Cell Model Passports. Their academic-use, access, and snapshot conditions remain documented; upstream services still require network access and may impose limits. Agents discover relevant tools before calling them. Full tool schemas are loaded as needed instead of being included in every turn. The scientific MCP catalog documents the connectors, tool capabilities, upstream sources, and usage conditions. Connections and Tool Details Settings → Connections shows bilingual connector introductions, maintainers, and source/documentation links. Expand a tool to inspect its description, parameter types, required fields, defaults, and full schema. Output schemas and examples appear when supplied by the service. Per-tool allow/ask/deny controls remain accessible while browsing details. Project-wide approval modes now live in Settings → Permissions. Plugin MCP processes on Windows receive the user-profile environment variables needed by their local dependencies. Setup, Settings, and Skills Local runtimes are optional during onboarding. Quick setup detects local tools and supports editing executable paths; keyboard navigation and error-card layout are more reliable. Local environment and network settings are grouped under General. Separate proxy settings cover model APIs, MCP services, and local code; package-mirror guidance can be configured for environment installation. Credentials use service detail pages, and Skills gain a catalog and package detail browser. Settings layouts keep controls reachable in smaller windows. The app and documentation adopt SpicyChicken6's three-wisp icon and wordmark. Python/R Runtime Reliability Python script execution preserves script semantics, and runtime execution guidance is clearer. Internal runtime generation guards stay out of model-facing tool schemas. Skills can declare Python and R runtime sidecars through a consistent convention. Bundled helper paths, retrieval error handling, and loading side effects are corrected. The public data acquisition skill includes optional geokit guidance. The bundled models.dev catalog is refreshed for current model limits, capabilities, and pricing metadata. title: Time-reversal SMOTE: An Oversampling Algorithm Based on Time-Reversal Evolution Rules
abstract: Classifying imbalanced data remains a ubiquitous and formidable challenge in machine learning and data mining. Traditional oversampling methods, represented by the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and its variants, primarily rely on linear interpolation based on Euclidean distances within the feature space. These approaches frequently overlook the underlying dynamic evolutionary laws of data, which tends to generate synthetic samples that deviate from the true data distribution, thereby triggering overfitting or concept drift. To address these deficiencies, this paper proposes a novel oversampling algorithm termed Time-reversal SMOTE, which incorporates time-reversal evolution rules. Departing from the conventional forward-generative mindset of "inferring effects from causes," the algorithm innovatively establishes a backward-inference mechanism that "traces data generation paths from observed results." By introducing a time-reversal operator and evolutionary trajectory constraints, the algorithm treats the existing minority class samples as the terminal states of evolution. It then reversely deduces their generative sources and intermediate evolutionary trajectories further upstream on the timeline, substantially reconstructing the dynamic continuity of the data. Theoretical analysis indicates that Time-reversal SMOTE can generate high-fidelity samples with greater rationality in both feature distribution and dynamic structures. Consequently, this method effectively preserves the underlying topological manifolds, eliminates boundary blur, and significantly enhances the classification accuracy and generalization capabilities of downstream classifiers on imbalanced datasets.

title: Hierarchical Abstraction SMOTE: A Layered Over-Sampling Algorithm Based on Low-Mid-High Abstraction
abstract: In the fields of machine learning and data mining, classification on imbalanced data presents a classic yet highly challenging problem. The traditional Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) generates new samples via linear interpolation between nearest neighbors. However, this approach ignores the underlying topological structures and multi-scale features of the data, making it prone to introducing noise and causing overfitting. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling algorithm named Hierarchical Abstraction SMOTE (HA-SMOTE). By constructing a "low-mid-high" hierarchical abstraction architecture, the algorithm comprehensively captures the microscopic local geometry, mesoscopic manifold distribution, and macroscopic global semantics of the minority class data. In the low-level abstraction, local density and boundary distributions are computed using local neighborhood relationships. In the mid-level abstraction, a tree-like manifold structure of the data is built through agglomerative hierarchical clustering to capture multi-scale features of boundary and core clusters. In the high-level abstraction, the global centroid and macroscopic weights of each cluster are calculated to characterize the overall distribution boundaries of the minority class. Finally, the algorithm utilizes this hierarchical structure to guide the step-by-step generation of new samples, prioritizing multi-scale interpolation within sparse and representative mid-level manifold branches. Structural analysis indicates that HA-SMOTE effectively preserves the continuity of complex data manifolds while enhancing the discriminative power of the decision boundary.

title: Evaluation Rigor from Graph Neural Networks to Graph Foundation Models: A Systematic Review and a Four-Axis Reporting Standard
abstract: Graph machine learning reports steady progress across node, graph, and link prediction, across temporal and hypergraph frontiers, and across the emerging class of graph foundation models. This review asks a prior question: when a method is reported to outperform the alternatives, how far does the evidence support the claim? We organize the answer around four axes of evaluation rigor: statistical rigor (seeds, dispersion, formal significance testing), baseline fairness (budget-parity tuning of trivial and structure-agnostic baselines), data integrity (leakage, duplication, negative sampling, contamination), and claim integrity (whether gains survive fair tuning and discriminative benchmarks). Drawing on a criterion-based corpus of 150 studies, of which 51 were read in full depth, we find a consistent picture. Only two of 25 methodologically central backbone studies apply a formal between-method significance test, and reported gains repeatedly shrink or disappear once a trivial baseline is tuned to parity, a leaked split is repaired, or a pretrained model is evaluated on unseen data. We argue that these failures share one cause: the saturation of benchmarks that can no longer discriminate between methods. The principal output is a minimum reporting standard, a concrete four-axis checklist that authors and reviewers can apply at negligible cost.

title: Distributed named entity recognition using parallel MapReduce and Stanford NER
abstract: Distributed named entity recognition using parallel MapReduce and Stanford NER occupies a distinctive place in the history of large-scale text analytics. The topic sits at the intersection of classical conditional-random-field sequence labeling, batch-oriented distributed computing, and contemporary demands for corpus-scale information extraction. This review examines recent journal literature relevant to that intersection, particularly the declining visibility of explicit Hadoop MapReduce implementations and the continuing analytical relevance of Stanford-style pipeline design. The review argues that the current literature contains few direct reimplementation of Stanford NER on MapReduce clusters; instead, the most relevant evidence comes from adjacent journal work on scalable biomedical, clinical, and domain-specific entity-extraction systems, which helps explain what aspects of the older architecture remain technically relevant and which have been displaced by Spark-native, toolkit-based, or transformer-based systems. Key themes include batch partitioning, model portability, inference locality, deployment economics, annotation normalization, and the tension between throughput and contextual richness. The review suggests that a major gap is the scarcity of direct peer-reviewed journal studies on Hadoop MapReduce and Stanford NER from 2020 onward. This scarcity is itself evidence of a field shift: away from explicit MapReduce orchestration and toward resource-centered toolchains and high-capacity neural inference.

title: Online Linear Programming for Multi-Objective Routing in LLM Serving
abstract: We study the online routing problem in large language model serving, where requests arrive sequentially and must be dispatched to parallel decode workers under tight batch-size and KV-cache constraints. Unlike widely used routing heuristics that are not tied to explicit service-level objectives (SLOs) and offer limited control over latency-throughput trade-offs, we introduce a multi-objective optimization framework that formulates routing as an online linear programming with interpretable decision rewards. We apply an efficient bid-price control policy based on the online linear programming that admits requests when their SLO-weighted benefit exceeds their shadow prices. To meet millisecond decision requirements, we develop a warm-started, projected first-order updates that track the evolving dual shadow prices online with predictable runtime. We integrate our router into the Vidur simulator and demonstrate substantial improvements over standard baselines across multiple SLO regimes, including end-to-end latency, time-to-first-token, throughput, and tail performance. A big picture from our result: a science-based approach outperforms others based on heuristics.
